questions.question: What property must a material have for particles of a liquid to move through it by diffusion?
options: It must be completely solid and non-porous.
It must be permeable.
It must be magnetic.
It must be impermeable.

questions.question: Which of the following is an observation made when a liquid diffuses into a jelly cube?
options: The liquid evaporates immediately upon touching the jelly.
The liquid moves into and spreads through the jelly cube.
The jelly cube instantly dissolves into a gas.
The jelly cube expands to ten times its original size.

questions.question: What is the expected effect of a higher temperature on the diffusion of a liquid into a jelly cube?
options: Diffusion slows down.
Diffusion stops completely.
Diffusion happens faster.
The temperature has no effect on diffusion.

questions.question: How does the size of a jelly cube affect the observed diffusion of a liquid into its center?
options: The liquid reaches the center of a smaller cube faster than a larger cube.
The liquid reaches the center of a larger cube faster than a smaller cube.
Cube size has no effect on how long it takes to reach the center.
Diffusion only occurs in the largest possible cubes.

questions.question: Using the particle model, why does a higher temperature increase the rate of diffusion into a jelly cube?
options: Particles gain kinetic energy and move faster.
Particles lose mass and become lighter.
Particles stop colliding with each other.
The jelly cube particles become larger.

questions.question: Why are particles of some substances able to pass through a selectively-permeable membrane?
options: They are attracted by magnetic forces in the membrane.
They are small enough to pass through the holes in the membrane.
They are made of a different state of matter.
They dissolve the membrane to create large openings.

questions.question: In which direction do particles of a substance move through a selectively-permeable membrane?
options: They move only from the outside to the inside.
They move only from the inside to the outside.
They move in both directions across the membrane.
They only travel along the outer surface without entering.

questions.question: If there is a higher concentration of a substance on one side of a selectively-permeable membrane than the other, what is the predicted direction of net movement?
options: From the area of lower concentration to higher concentration.
From the area of higher concentration to lower concentration.
There will be no movement of particles at all.
Particles will move sideways only, avoiding the membrane.

questions.question: In an experiment using Visking tubing to observe diffusion, what can typically be seen when starch-indicator iodine is placed outside the tubing?
options: The iodine particles remain completely stationary outside.
The iodine particles diffuse through the tubing, turning the inside solution blue-black.
The starch particles diffuse out and turn the outer solution blue-black.
The tubing completely dissolves due to the iodine.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the composition of the cell cytoplasm and its substances?
options: They are continuous fluids that are not made of particles.
They are made up of particles, just like all other substances.
They contain only energy waves and no matter.
They are made of a single giant macromolecule with no individual parts.

questions.question: How do particles of certain substances enter and leave a cell?
options: By passing through small holes in the cell membrane.
By destroying the cell membrane.
By being actively pulled through solid lipids.
By turning into a gas to bypass the membrane.

questions.question: Why are some substances unable to diffuse through the holes in a cell membrane?
options: Their particles are too small to be noticed.
The particles that make them up are too big.
They do not have enough magnetic charge.
Their particles are converted into water.

questions.question: Why is the cell membrane described as selectively-permeable?
options: It allows all substances to pass through without any restriction.
Only some substances can diffuse through it.
It completely blocks all substances from entering or leaving.
It only allows liquids to pass through, blocking all gases.

questions.question: What is the direction of the net movement of particles through a cell membrane?
options: Up a concentration gradient.
Down a concentration gradient.
Against the concentration gradient.
Sideways along the membrane gradient.

questions.question: How do particles of a substance behave during diffusion?
options: They move in a perfectly synchronized straight line.
They move in random directions and collide all the time.
They remain stationary and vibrate in fixed positions.
They only move when a force of gravity pulls them.

questions.question: In science, how is 'concentration' defined?
options: The physical size of a single particle.
The total speed of particles moving in a container.
The number of particles in a volume of liquid or gas.
The strength of the chemical bonds inside a molecule.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the process of diffusion?
options: The active transport of particles using cellular energy.
The passive movement of particles from an area of higher to lower concentration.
The evaporation of water from a semi-permeable surface.
The chemical bonding of two different substances.
